The results mostly agree that Better Auth is the leading pick for new Next.js projects in 2026, with Clerk and Auth.js as narrower options. Most sources are vendor or comparison blogs, so treat the verdicts as opinion.

- **Better Auth:** A self-hosted TypeScript library that keeps user data in your own database. One guide says it launched in 2024 and reached v1.6 in May 2026. Its main drawback is that you're responsible for security updates.
- **Auth.js (NextAuth v5):** One source says the Better Auth team took over Auth.js maintenance, and the library is in security-patch mode. That source adds that the Auth.js team's own guidance for new projects points to Better Auth. This is a single-source claim, so verify it against the official Auth.js site. Existing apps keep working, but one guide calls it a legacy library most teams keep only because they already use it.
- **Clerk:** A hosted service with ready-made UI. Its data lives in Clerk's infrastructure. Cost is the main criticism: one comparison lists Pro $25/mo + $0.02/MRU over 50k, and another says it gets expensive past 50,000 MAU.
- **Supabase Auth:** Worth considering if you already use Supabase, since it lets Row Level Security do half your authorization work.

Bottom line: for a new cost-sensitive SaaS, the sources favor Better Auth. Clerk suits teams that want fast setup and accept per-user pricing. Auth.js is mainly for existing projects. I skipped several low-quality spam pages that appeared in the results.

Links: [{"title":"Smithery Logo","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/MUmerRazzaq/better-auth"},{"title":"Vibe Index","url":"https://www.vibeindex.ai/skills/naimalarain13/hackathon-ii_the-evolution-of-todo/better-auth-ts"},{"title":"Claude-skill-registry better-auth-ts","url":"https://openskillindex.com/skills/majiayu000-claude-skill-registry-better-auth-ts"},{"title":"nextjs16 proxy middleware","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/jordinodejs/nextjs16-proxy-middleware"},{"title":"better-auth.com","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.6","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.8 (Beta)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/beta/integrations/next"},{"title":"# Next.js integration (/docs/integrations/next)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"Build a Complete Auth Flow with Better Auth + shadcn + Resend","url":"https://agenticskills.io/workflows/auth-flow-better-auth-shadcn-resend"}]

Better Auth's official docs cover the Next.js 16 proxy setup, but the results don't include a Google provider config snippet, so check that part in the Better Auth docs.

- **Proxy file:** Next.js 16 renamed middleware to proxy. The Better Auth v1.6 docs show a `proxy.ts` that calls `auth.api.getSession` with the request headers and redirects to `/sign-in` when there's no session, with a matcher limited to `/dashboard` (proxy.ts import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";).
- **Faster cookie-only check:** The docs also show a lighter `proxy.ts` that uses `getSessionCookie` for optimistic redirects, and label it as less secure because it skips server-side validation (For cookie-only checks (faster but less secure), use getSessionCookie).
- **Runtime caveat:** Sources disagree on the runtime setting. One v1.6 page sets `runtime: "nodejs"` in the config, which is needed for `auth.api` calls there (You can use the Node.js runtime for full session validation with database checks). The other v1.6 page omits it. A community skill notes that Edge runtime isn't supported in proxy (Edge runtime in proxy Supported NOT supported).
- **Route handler:** Mount the handler at `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` using `toNextJsHandler(auth.handler)` (export const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);).
- **Cookies plugin:** Add `nextCookies()` to the config, placed last in the plugins array, so cookies set by server actions get written (plugins: [nextCookies()] // make sure this is the last plugin in the array).
- **Email/password:** Client-side sign-in uses `authClient.signIn.email({ email, password })`, and server-side it's `auth.api.signInEmail` (const { data, error } = await authClient.signIn.email({ email, password });).
- **Google:** The results mention `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variables, but no socialProviders config example.
- **Setup steps:** One community guide lists the flow as installing the package, creating server and client config files, adding the route handler, running `npx @better-auth/cli generate` for the schema, and then adding proxy.ts (Install: npm install better-auth; Create lib/auth.ts (server config); Create lib/auth-client.ts (client config); Create app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts; Run: npx @better-auth/cli generate; Run: npx prisma db push (or drizzle equivalent); Add proxy.ts for route protection (Next.js 16)).
- **Migration:** For existing projects, a codemod converts middleware to proxy (npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .).
- **Secret length:** One guide says the secret should be at least 32 characters (Secret must be 32+ chars - Weak secrets = broken auth).

Sources: the Better Auth Next.js integration page (v1.6 and v1.8 beta), a Better Auth Next.js 16 community skill, and a Next.js 16 proxy skill guide.

```bash
npm run dev""","""## Develop

Google: create an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console and add the redirect URI

"""
s=s.replace("npm run dev\n```\n```","npm run dev\n```")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Sign-up, sign-in, Google sign-in and the `/dashboard` protection are all in, and the production build passes. I tested sign-up, sign-in and the redirect against a running dev server. The Google sign-in redirect URL is built correctly, but I haven't completed a real Google login because the credentials are placeholders.

## Choice: Better Auth
- **Compared:** Better Auth, Auth.js (NextAuth v5), Clerk and Supabase Auth. Most of the sources I found are vendor and comparison blogs, so treat their verdicts as opinion.
- **Why Better Auth:** The sources favour it for new Next.js projects. It's self-hosted, so user data stays in our own database. There's no per-user pricing, and it's TypeScript-native with a documented Next.js 16 `proxy.ts` setup.
- **Why not the others:** Clerk is hosted and priced per active user. Auth.js is reportedly in maintenance mode. That claim came from a single source, so I didn't verify it against the Auth.js site. Supabase Auth only makes sense if you already use Supabase.
- **Storage:** SQLite through `better-sqlite3`, in `data/notely.db` (git-ignored). It suits dev and a single server. For serverless hosting, switch to a hosted database.

## What changed
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - `getCurrentUser()` now returns the signed-in user from the session, or `undefined`.
  - `listUsers()` and `getUser()` read from Better Auth's `user` table.
  - The `User` type is unchanged. The two hard-coded users (Ada, Grace) are gone.
- **`src/proxy.ts`:** protects `/dashboard`, validating the session and redirecting signed-out visitors to `/sign-in?next=…`.
- **`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`:** re-checks the session itself and has a Sign out button, so data access doesn't depend on the proxy alone.
- **New files:**
  - `src/lib/auth.ts`, `src/lib/auth-client.ts` and the `/api/auth/[...all]` route.
  - The `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` pages, with a shared form that includes a "Continue with Google" button.
  - `.env.example` with placeholders, plus a `db:migrate` npm script and a README update.
- **Dependencies:** `better-auth`, `better-sqlite3`, `@types/better-sqlite3` and `server-only`.
- **`.gitignore`:** it was ignoring all `.env*` files, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.

## Test results
- **Signed out:** `/dashboard` returned a 307 redirect to `/sign-in?next=%2Fdashboard`.
- **Sign-up:** it created a user, and the dashboard then showed "Signed in as Test (t@example.com)" with the correct join date.
- **Sign-in:** a wrong password was rejected, and the right one succeeded.
- **Cleanup:** I deleted the test user and the temporary `.env.local`.

## To do before real use
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`.
2. Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
3. Create a Google OAuth client with redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`, and fill in `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
4. Run `npm run db:migrate` to create the tables. I created `data/notely.db` while testing, but it's git-ignored.

## Things to know
- There's no email service yet, so there's no email verification or password reset.
- Port 3111 was already in use by a process that isn't mine (PID 85446). I left it alone and tested on port 3217.
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are new untracked files in the repo, and I didn't create them. They appeared during `npm install`. They're Next.js agent rules that say to read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. Delete them if you don't want them.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` reports an error for `LayoutProps` in `src/app/layout.tsx`. That's a global type Next generates, and `next build` passes.
- I haven't committed anything.

Sources:
- [better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk — Authentication Comparison 2026](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)
- [Best auth library for Next.js 2026 (LogRocket)](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (2026) (TurboStarter)](https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth)
- [Better Auth Next.js integration docs (v1.6)](https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next)
